# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Excellus BlueCross BlueShield — Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
By phone: the Customer Care number on my member card

**From:** Jordan Mercado
Member ID: W484245232
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-11 — Reference number POC-FD00FECEC4-98407**
**Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Governing policy:** Excellus BlueCross BlueShield Medical Policy 7.01.96 Hip Arthroplasty (https://www.excellusbcbs.com/documents/d/global/exc-prv-hip-arthroplasty-effective-on-2026-02-16-)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which Excellus BlueCross BlueShield denied on 2026-08-11 under reference number POC-FD00FECEC4-98407. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before the requested surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider, because the records in my file do document exactly the non-surgical care the plan's own policy describes.

My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this procedure is needed. Below I have set the plan's published criteria side by side with what is already in my chart.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

**1. Non-surgical management.** Medical Policy 7.01.96 Hip Arthroplasty states:

> "3. Failure of at least three (3) months of provider- directed non-surgical management;*"

My records show non-surgical management directed by my providers that runs well past three months:

- **Supervised physical therapy:** 12 weeks, from 2026-04-04 to 2026-06-27, with 20 visits completed, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-03, which gave 2 weeks of partial relief.

That is a course of provider-directed, non-surgical treatment lasting longer than three months, and it failed to resolve my symptoms. The policy also contains an exception to this requirement:

> "*Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider -directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider -directed non-surgical management inappropriate."

I do not need to rely on that exception, because the three months of treatment actually happened and are documented. I note it only to show that the policy's focus is on whether non-surgical care was genuinely tried or genuinely unsuitable — and in my case it was tried, at length, and did not work.

**2. Function-limiting pain.** The policy states:

> "a. Function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration; *"

My records document 14 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. I walk with a cane and I am limited to one block. That is a shorter distance than the examples the policy itself gives, and it has gone on far longer than three months. The policy also allows:

> "*Criteria exception: Three (3) months of function -limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate;"

Again, I meet the duration requirement on its face at 14 months.

**3. Loss of hip function.** The policy states:

> "b. Loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age -appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment; AND"

My records document that I cannot put on my shoes unassisted, that I ambulate with a cane, and that my walking is limited to one block. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. Dressing myself and walking are ordinary daily activities, and the chart shows both are affected.

**4. Imaging.** The policy states:

> "B. Osteoarthritis, Avascular Necrosis (AVN), Inflammatory Arthritis 1. Imaging shows ANY of the following findings:"

and lists, among those findings:

> "a. Tönnis Grade two (2) -three (3) osteoarthritis;"

My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph of 2026-07-14 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. The records I have do not state a Tönnis grade in those words. If the plan's review turns on that grading, I ask that it request the grading from Dr. Lindqvist rather than deny the request for a missing label, particularly since the denial notice did not identify imaging as the reason for the decision.

**5. Other criteria.** My records also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## What I am asking for

The plan's policy contains additional conditions and lists that were not reproduced in the material I have, so I cannot address every element of it point by point. If the plan continues to deny this request, I ask that it identify in writing the specific criterion from Medical Policy 7.01.96 Hip Arthroplasty that it applied and the specific document or finding it found missing, so that Dr. Lindqvist and I can respond to it directly.

The denial notice gave one reason: an inadequate trial of conservative treatment. My chart contains 12 weeks and 20 visits of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection that gave only two weeks of partial relief — all before surgery was requested. I respectfully ask the plan to overturn this denial and authorize CPT 27130.

Please treat this letter as my formal appeal. My appeal is due by 2027-02-07, and I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; I understand I may also reach the plan by phone at the Customer Care number on my member card.

I am happy to authorize the release of any additional records. Dr. Lindqvist's office can be reached at [surgeon's office phone number] and can provide the physical therapy discharge note, the imaging report of 2026-07-14, and the operative plan on request.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Mercado**
Member ID: W484245232
Reference number: POC-FD00FECEC4-98407
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [List what you send — e.g., physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-06-27; radiology report dated 2026-07-14; office notes from Dr. Lindqvist; copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-11]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
